ideas.pitch: AI-powered medical triage and symptom checker designed specifically for college health centers.
ideas.title: CampusCare AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Follows the Clinical-Simulator pattern by targeting a highly relatable institutional vertical with measurable scoring rubrics that impress academic judges.

ideas.pitch: GPS-enabled civic reporting tool that automatically bundles community pothole and infrastructure complaints into verified municipal repair tickets.
ideas.title: CivicRoute
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors the catwalk win by combining real-world local impact with a live map dashboard that judges can interact with instantly during the offline finale.

ideas.pitch: App that coordinates local undergraduate student volunteers to drive and accompany nearby seniors on essential social outings.
ideas.title: ElderLink
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly inspired by the Vanderbilt Global Good Hackathon grand prize winner, focusing on social good and community building which strongly resonates with undergraduate engineering panels.

ideas.pitch: Sixty-second voice biomarker screening tool optimized for early detection of neurological fatigue or cognitive decline.
ideas.title: VoiceCheck
ideas.why_it_could_win: Employs the exact winning formula of the Antrophic Hackathon winner by showcasing a fast, impressive AI audio diagnostic demo within a 24-hour build window.

ideas.pitch: Autonomous multi-agent system that ingests emergency messages, cross-references local resource availability, and drafts optimized dispatch plans.
ideas.title: CrisisDispatch Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages the agentic disaster response pattern seen in the AI Agents Hackathon win, demonstrating hard engineering with autonomous loops that stand out against standard CRUD apps.
